summary: AutoIndex searches over Python document-preprocessing programs (chunking, section reweighting, LaTeX stripping, enrichment) for a fixed BM25 retriever. An analysis agent with read-only bm25_retrieve/read_file/grep tools diagnoses failures on stratified validation queries; a code agent proposes 4 candidate programs per iteration, and a candidate is kept only if validation Recall@100 improves (5 iterations). On CRUMB's 8 retrieval tasks (1:2 validation/held-out query split), qwen3-coder (3 seeds) averages +8.4% relative Recall@100 and +8.3% nDCG@10 over full-document BM25, with gains concentrated on 3 splits. This is an information-retrieval paper, not about software development with agents.

claims.claim: Average gains of +8.4% Recall@100 and +8.3% nDCG@10 over full-document BM25
claims.evidence: Tables 1-2 (held-out queries, qwen3-coder, mean of 3 seeds): macro R@100 30.1 -> 32.6. Gains are driven by SetOpEntity (+30.5%), TheoremRetrieval (+19.2%) and LegalQA (+10.4%), where seed std is large (LQA +/-6.0, SOE +/-5.8). Sonnet 4.6 (2 seeds, two splits single-seed) gives +6.8% (Table 4).

claims.claim: Learned programs improve recall on all 8 tasks
claims.evidence: PaperRetrieval 33.7 -> 33.7 (+0.1%), ClinicalTrial +2.1%, CodeRetrieval 4.7 -> 5.0. Sonnet improves only 7/8 (TipOfTongue +0.0%), and nDCG@10 falls on TipOfTongue and PaperRetrieval. 'All 8' counts noise-level deltas as wins.

claims.claim: Iteration, search history and grounded failure analysis each contribute
claims.evidence: Table 3 (qwen3-coder, 3 runs): 1 iteration -> 3/8 splits positive; without analysis agent -> 6/8 positive with smaller gains; without history -> 5/8 positive, yet close to full on CodeRetrieval (+5.9 vs +6.5) and above it on StackExchange (+4.7 vs +4.1), so the history effect is mixed.

claims.claim: Learned representations transfer to dense retrieval
claims.evidence: One experiment on StackExchange with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B: R@100 0.739 -> 0.874. No other split or embedder.

claims.claim: AutoIndex outperforms domain-agnostic uniform chunking by large margins (+42% to +361%)
claims.evidence: The CRUMB 512-token passage baseline is far below full-document BM25 on every split (e.g., TipOfTongue 5.8 vs 25.0), so relative deltas against it are inflated. No tuned chunk-size/overlap grid, BM25F field weighting, or doc2query comparison.

patterns.note: Validation-gated LLM search over preprocessing code beats static untuned BM25 baselines on average, but gains are near zero on 2-3 of 8 splits and it is never compared to a tuned heuristic search (chunk grid, BM25F) or to RAG-pipeline optimizers.
BM25 is the fixed substrate. The paper improves the lexical index's input, not lexical vs semantic retrieval. The CodeRetrieval gain is negligible in absolute terms (4.7 -> 5.0 R@100).

Read-only analysis agent separated from the code agent to keep the code agent's context clean (A.2). The 'w/o analysis' ablation removes diagnosis entirely, so it does not isolate the separation itself.

methodology.sample: CRUMB: 8 retrieval splits (held-out queries 51-4,569 per split), 1:2 validation/evaluation query split
methodology.baselines: Full-document BM25; CRUMB 512-token passage corpus. No tuned chunking grid, field weighting, doc2query or AutoRAG-style optimizer
methodology.models: qwen3-coder (3 seeds) and Claude Sonnet 4.6 (2 seeds; 2 splits single-seed) as code-agent backbones; bm25s Lucene BM25
methodology.variance: Mean +/- std over 2-3 seeds; no significance tests
methodology.ablations: 1 iteration, without search history, without analysis agent (qwen3-coder only)
methodology.contamination_controls: Held-out query split per corpus. Prompts were refined on early runs (A.2) on the same benchmark, splits unspecified
methodology.languages: English text corpora; one code-retrieval split

standards.artifacts: Code on GitHub (auto-index/autoindex); prompts and query splits in appendix

biases.detail: Per-corpus optimization on one benchmark, with prompts iterated on early runs of the same benchmark.
The passage-corpus baseline is much weaker than full-document BM25 and is used for +100-400% relative claims. No tuned heuristic baseline.
2-3 seeds with large per-split std on the splits that carry the average.

coi.detail: Vendor affiliation of one author only. No Databricks product is evaluated.

verdict_reason: Off-topic: a retrieval-indexing optimization study on a general IR benchmark, not about software development with LLM agents or its human side. The method is reasonably evaluated (seeds, ablations, held-out queries, released code), but 'improves all 8 tasks' counts noise-level deltas, and the large relative gains over the passage baseline are against a weak baseline.
applicability: Does not transfer to the discovery/onboarding harness. It needs a labeled query-to-document relevance set per corpus, which the team does not have for its code, specs or Confluence-style docs. The code-retrieval split gain is negligible. If the team later builds lexical search over the domain with real seed queries (e.g., logged onboarding questions), an offline, validation-gated preprocessing search adds no query-time LLM cost. That is a retrieval-tuning idea, not a harness decision.
